help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: Why the choices change: Permanently failed sources, services that are off, unavailable, out of quota or not included in the plan, and completed downloads drop out of the list or are shown as unavailable. Switching back and forth several times does not by itself remove a choice.

Progress: if choosing a source would discard progress already made, DebridPulse first asks Discard downloaded progress?. A service switch that would discard progress is refused instead, and the reason shown is Switching would discard downloaded data; to confirm, switch that link's source.

While a download is paused: If you choose a different source for a file that has already started downloading, the choice is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The displayed service and source stay as the current ones, and a message next to the service name shows where the file will move to (for example, Switch to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume). Choosing again changes this message, and choosing the source already in use makes the message disappear. On resume it shows Switching to … until the switch is applied, then disappears. If the paused files of a download move to different places or the destination is unknown, no destination is shown. A file that has never started has nothing to hand over, so the new source simply applies when the file starts. Choosing a Service while paused behaves as described above, but the download stays paused. A service that can handle the link in use takes over immediately (shown on the badge); a service that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing… and takes over only after you resume. These messages appear in the download activity and on the download's row, and both kinds can appear at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. While it is on, that service also adds torrents that another service is delivering, so it is ready to take over when needed, and when a download is switched to another service it keeps the torrent it already started as a backup instead of removing it. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits, and when a new download that needs a slot arrives, the new download takes the slot a backup was using first. Turn it off to keep that service's slots for its own downloads; in that case the backups are removed. Choices you already saved are kept.

help.howitworks.adding_same_thing.if_add.backTranslation: If you add a magnet, {file_type}, NZB or Metalink file that DebridPulse is already handling (including items that failed but were not removed), Already in queue is shown and the existing download is kept without starting a second one. Web links are always added as a new download. Adding the same source again after the download has completed, been cancelled or been removed starts a new download. help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts shows each person's role, sign-in method and whether the account is enabled. Add local account creates an account that signs in with a username and password. A role changed in Edit user takes effect immediately; pages that user has open are not signed out but reload with the new role. Everyone has a DebridPulse username separate from the display name. OIDC accounts receive this name at first sign-in, and it is the name used when signing in with a local password. You can change this name with the pencil icon next to the name in the Edit user title, and the saved password is kept. Clicking an account name shows its details and activity, where you can withdraw pending requests individually. Disable and Remove first show how many pending download requests the account has. These requests are withdrawn, but transfers that someone else also requested continue, and completed downloads are never affected. Disabling also ends the account's sign-ins and stops its tokens. Removing keeps the account's records and deletes the account's notification settings. If a removed OIDC sign-in comes back, a new account is created, and it stays disabled until you enable it yourself. Merge combines two or more accounts into the one account you choose to keep. If two accounts share a verified email you are told about it, but they are actually combined only when you run a merge. DebridPulse always keeps at least one usable administrator, and you cannot change your own role or disable your own account.

help.settings.data_maintenance.backups.backTranslation: Backups opens the list of backups. Select a backup to Save backup (download a copy), Restore backup or Remove it, and Add backup checks a copy you saved and then uploads it. Restoring pauses processing, makes a safety backup of the current state, checks the selected backup again, then replaces the current database and settings and restarts the DebridPulse service. If the check fails nothing is changed, and any pause you set yourself or an *arr client set returns to its original state.

help.settings.data_maintenance.backups_r.backTranslation: Backups and retention: Creates scheduled backups in the Backup folder (on by default), and Additional backup and retention settings has Backup interval, Backup retention period and Maximum backups kept. A backup is removed when it is too old or no longer among the newest backups kept. The same section also sets how often Statistics snapshots are made and how long they are kept. A statistics snapshot is a record of the previous 24 hours of activity, stored inside the DebridPulse database. Snapshots are not reports, are not sent anywhere, and cannot be viewed in the current interface. Run backup creates a backup right now (only when backups are enabled).

help.settings.data_maintenance.database_.backTranslation: Database reset controls: turn on Allow database reset, press Reset database, then type {literal} and press Delete entire database. This deletes all downloads and their requests and records, events and statistics snapshots. Accounts, passwords, OIDC account links, API tokens, personal notification settings and all settings are kept. DebridPulse always makes a safety backup first, and if that backup fails the operation stops. During the reset it stops running downloads and pauses processing, and when the reset is finished it returns to the previous pause state. Completed files already in the download folder are not deleted.

help.trouble.before_changing_anything.av.backTranslation: Do not remove a download only for the purpose of clearing an error. DebridPulse keeps a download's source and history so that it can retry or recover. If you need help, the Transfer Trace Log in Details (admin only) lets you save a record that does not include passwords or private link details. Read the content before sharing it. Never share API keys or tokens, and never share links that contain passwords either.

help.topic.user_accounts.roles.readonly_.backTranslation: Read-only user: Can view downloads and statistics, but cannot add, change or remove anything.

help.topic.user_accounts.account_actions.backTranslation: Disabling an account ends that account's sessions and withdraws its pending download requests. Removing an account does the same, and also deletes that account's notification settings.

help.topic.integration_accounts.tokens.r.backTranslation: Pressing 'Revoke' makes that token immediately unusable for authentication. Jobs are not withdrawn.

help.topic.integration_accounts.what_int.backTranslation: It cannot directly pause, delete or redirect transfers, change settings, or see other clients' work.

help.topic.integration_accounts.disable_.backTranslation: Deleting the account also permanently revokes its token.

help.topic.delivery_profiles.jobs_files..backTranslation: Submitting a job creates a download request belonging to that application. Removing the job in the application withdraws that request, or, if delivery has already completed, treats the delivery as acknowledged. The transfer itself stops only when no one else needs it.
Completed files are shared in place. Nothing is copied, linked or moved for the application, and files are not deleted when a delivery is acknowledged or expires.

help.topic.deployment_type.standalone.wi.backTranslation: Without a password, no sign-in is required, and you use DebridPulse as the built-in Administrator.

help.topic.deployment_type.what_switchin.backTranslation: No account is deleted. Other people's accounts keep their usernames, passwords, identity provider links and saved enabled or disabled state as they are. In Standalone they cannot sign in regardless of that state.
Switching clears the built-in Administrator's password, turns off username-and-password sign-in and OpenID Connect sign-in, and ends all browser sessions.

Afterwards no sign-in is required. Anyone who can reach DebridPulse at an address DebridPulse allows can use DebridPulse as the built-in administrator. This is not limited to this computer, and it does not expire.

help.topic.backups.backups.while_enable.backTranslation: While 'Enable' is on, a backup is made every 'Backup interval', and pressing 'Run backup' makes one right now. 'Backups' lists the saved backups, where you can add, save, restore or remove a backup.

help.topic.backups.backups.backup.backTranslation: A backup is deleted when it becomes older than the 'Backup retention period' or no longer falls within the 'Maximum backups kept' among the newest backups, whichever comes first.

help.topic.backups.backups.older_backups.backTranslation: Older backups are deleted according to the saved retention rule, and this rule keeps applying. That setting is included in the Advanced display mode.

help.topic.backups.statistics_snapshots..backTranslation: Separately, every 'Statistics snapshot interval' DebridPulse saves a record of the previous 24 hours of activity inside its own database, and deletes snapshots older than the 'Statistics snapshot retention period'. Setting it to 0 stops new snapshots from being made.

help.topic.database_reset.intro.erases_d.backTranslation: Erases DebridPulse's download records so it starts again from an empty state. Use it only if you want to start over from the beginning.

help.topic.heading.what_removed_kept.backTranslation: What is removed and what is kept

help.topic.database_reset.what_removed_k.backTranslation: Removed: records of transfers and their files, download requests, external jobs, events and the activity log, statistics snapshots.
Kept: accounts, passwords, OpenID Connect links, API tokens, personal notification settings, and all settings. Files downloaded to disk are not deleted.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.res.backTranslation: 'Reset database' works only when 'Allow database reset' is on, and asks for confirmation.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.pro.backTranslation: During the reset, processing is paused and afterwards returns to its previous state. A safety backup is made first, and if the backup fails, nothing is erased.
